$comment: The presentation layer over their menu data. Every 'source' key here is a verbatim
'category > subcategory' pair read from menu_items (see scripts/ingest.mjs); nothing in this
file invents a dish, a price or a group. Where a display label differs from the source string
the source string is still printed in the item's provenance and in content/drift.md.
scripts/build-content.mjs fails the build if a source pair is missing here, if a family claims
a category twice, or if the section counts do not sum to the row count of the ingest.

families.label: Morning
families.line: The 6:30 opening is a real customer: chai, coffee, pastries and a full breakfast before the CBD fills the room.

families.label: Small plates
families.line: Starters, soups and the keto line — the part of the menu people order while the main table is still deciding.

families.label: The kitchen
families.line: Local and international, said literally: biryani and curries beside pasta, Thai fusion and Mexican.

families.label: Handheld
families.line: Shawarma in their own tortilla, sandwiches, burgers and wood-fired pizza.

families.label: The house
families.line: The goat dishes the reviews keep naming, and the children's menu.

families.label: The bar
families.line: A third of the menu is drink: 87 items across coffee, tea, lattes, cool specials, milkshakes, smoothies, dawas, nojitos, coladas and juices.

$sectionComment: source pair -> display label. Order here is the order sections appear on /menu.

Breakfast > Fruit Salad/Add-ons & Upgrad.label: Sides & add-ons
Breakfast > Fruit Salad/Add-ons & Upgrad.note: The source string calls this group Fruit Salad/Add-ons & Upgrades; the ten items in it are sides and upgrades, so the label says so.

Breakfast > CAKES.label: Celebration cakes
Breakfast > CAKES.note: Whole cakes sold by weight — 2KG and 3KG formats.

$tagComment: Tags are only ever set from a literal token in the item's own name, description, category or
subcategory. An empty match list means the tag is never asserted. build-content.mjs prints how
many items each rule touched, so an over-broad token is visible instead of silent.
